english.notes:
(i) The Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 were repealed by the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 as of 6th April 2025. For offences committed on or after that date see H101733.
(ii) The offence of misleading omission may arise when, for example, consumers are not given information they need to make informed choices (in relation to product). This occurs when commercial practices omit or hide material information, or provide it in an unclear, unintelligible, ambiguous or untimely manner and the average consumer takes, or is likely to take, a different decision as a result.
(iii) Office of Fair Trading guidance stated that a misleading omission can also occur where a trader fails to identify the commercial intent of a practice, if it is not already apparent from the context. The presence of a price, or of a statement making it clear that the practice is commercial (for example; "this is an advertisement"), are examples of how commercial intent could be made clear.
(iv) Material information is an important element of the offence. It is information that the average consumer needs to have, in the context, in order to make informed decisions. It includes any information required by European (EC) derived law, such as the Consumer Protection (Distance Selling) Regulations.

other.penalty:
Summary: fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see regulation 14 of the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
